citation.title: Zero-shot rib design: merging a training-free generative prior with topology optimization

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Across four domains and two physics regimes, 38 of 49 prompt-domain settings had significant compliance reductions against gradient-based baselines, with reported reductions up to 31.5% mechanical and 23.0% thermoelastic.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No faster-than-classical speed-up is claimed; Section 4 reports an SDS run about 3 minutes slower than pure SIMP, and Table 1's training-cost comparison concerns other learned methods.
claim.alternatives: Section 5.2/Table 6 compares best-run SDS compliance with tuned MMA and shows mixed results (SDS wins in Circle/Hole, MMA in Rect); Section 4 reports SDS runtime around 44 minutes versus 41 minutes for pure SIMP; Section 7/Table 11 reports a negative heat-conduction result.

baseline.classical_method: Sections 4-5: pure SIMP with Adam, tuned MMA, OC, 50-start SIMP, perturbation SIMP and image-guided SIMP; all use FE-based compliance.
baseline.implementation: Sections 3-4 and Appendix A: in-house Mindlin-Reissner MITC4 plate FE plus plane-stress FE, SIMP and Heaviside projection; Appendix D.8 uses FEniCSx for 3D re-analysis; implementation code on request.
baseline.hardware_classical: Section 4, p. 11: pure-SIMP baseline runtime reported beside SDS on NVIDIA RTX 4090 (24 GB VRAM); tuned MMA hardware not separately specified.
baseline.hardware_ml: Section 4, p. 11: NVIDIA RTX 4090 (24 GB VRAM).
baseline.problem_size: Table 3, p. 10: 150 x 150 FE elements for principal 2D domains; Appendix D.7 tests Hole at 100 x 100 and 200 x 200.
baseline.classical_iterations: Section 5.2/Table 6: Adam and MMA compared at a fixed 1,000 iterations under identical filtering and Heaviside continuation; Section 4/Table 3 specifies 1,000 for SDS.
baseline.classical_time: Section 4, p. 11: pure SIMP about 41 minutes per run [inferred from 44-minute SDS run and 3-minute overhead]; Section 5.2: tuned MMA 4.90 s/iteration.
baseline.ml_time: Section 4, p. 11: SDS about 44 minutes per 1,000-iteration run; Section 3 CAD conversion: about 5 seconds on one CPU core.
baseline.training_time: Sections 1 and 4: no task-specific training or fine-tuning; pretrained Stable Diffusion 2.1 stays frozen.
baseline.data_generation_cost: Sections 1 and 4: no task-specific training dataset; optimization itself uses FE analysis at every iteration.
baseline.quality_metric: Abstract and Tables 5-7: FE-computed mechanical/thermoelastic compliance at fixed target volume; Appendix D.8 gives 3D solid FE re-analysis of reconstructed rib geometry.
baseline.quality_gap: Abstract: up to 31.5% lower mechanical and 23.0% lower thermoelastic compliance; Section 5.2/Table 6: SDS best versus MMA is 7.886 vs 7.721 in Rect, 2.522 vs 2.598 in Circle, 43.20 vs 48.848 in Hole.

R1.evidence: Abstract, p. 1: primary outcome is compliance improvement at fixed volume; Section 4 reports SDS is slower than pure SIMP, so no faster-than-classical primary claim needs matching.

R2.evidence: Section 5.2/Table 6: tuned MMA and Adam are both tested; no re-test, per-iteration comparison against an independent strong solver, or established R2(a)-(e) condition is shown.

R3.evidence: Sections 1 and 4: pretrained diffusion weights remain frozen with no task-specific training or data-generation phase; the primary claim concerns quality.

R4.evidence: Sections 3-5 and Appendix B.3: final density compliance is evaluated by FE and target volume enforced by bisection; Appendix D.8 re-analyzes reconstructed solids, but disconnected/failed or post-CAD volume-violation rates are not counted.

reporting.n_test_cases: Abstract and Section 4: 245 primary SDS runs, 49 prompt-domain combinations across 4 geometric domains and 2 physics regimes; 5 random seeds per combination. Section 7 additionally tests heat conduction.

notes: Table 1 compares avoided training costs against other ML approaches, but the relevant classical comparison is quality. Section 5.2 reports a stronger MMA benchmark and acknowledges mixed best-run results; Section 7 gives a negative heat-conduction result. Data availability states numerical outputs can be reproduced from code and settings but code is available only on request, with no released result dataset.
